research.title: Permit Information | New Mexico Film Office
research.excerpt: Permit Information Although comparatively few permits are necessary for filming in New Mexico, permits are required for production on federal, state-owned, and tribal properties and lands. Permits are also often required for production on city properties, especially historical sites, and public streets, as well as for special use of county roads and state highways. \ Companies considering shooting on federal property must connect with the proper federal contact. Location Permits The New Mexico Film Office does not issue filming permits. Film permitting is generally handled by the city/town/county where you're filming. For permit questions specific to a location, please get in touch with the nearest film liaison. State-owned properties: Please contact the NMFO at 505-476-5600 or via email at info@nmfilm.com Railroad Right of Entry and Permitting Please get in touch with the NMDOT Rail Bureau NMDOT via email with any inquiries or questions about potential encroachment on railroad property. If you are within 100 feet of a railroad or between a fence/property marker and a railroad, you may be trespassing in the railroad right-of-way and can conflict with railroad operations which can create a serious safety hazard for the railroad and film production. This includes production at NM Rail Runner Express stations and Amtrak Stations. Filming activities may be interrupted if you fail to obtain written permission from the railroad owner to enter its property. In New Mexico, the three most prominent railroad property owners are BNSF Railway, Union Pacific Railroad, and the New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT). research.title: New Mexico Film Permits: 3 Important Permitting Facts - PPS
research.excerpt: This program provides a refundable tax credit for qualified production expenditures, which can significantly reduce the overall cost of filming in the state. The credit is available for both in-state and out-of-state productions, covering a wide range of eligible expenses, including labor costs, equipment rentals, and location fees. Filmmakers who meet the criteria for the program can benefit from a substantial rebate on their production spending. However, filmmakers must apply for the tax credit before filming begins, and the approval process is tied to the submission of detailed financial records, which must be provided for review. To film in New Mexico, filmmakers will still need to secure New Mexico film permits for filming in public areas or locations. These permits ensure that the production complies with local regulations, including safety and environmental protections, and allows access to public spaces like streets, parks, and other venues. The Southwestern aesthetic, with its distinct Native American and Spanish influences, is featured in films like The Milagro Beanfield War and The Book of Eli . Securing New Mexico film permits is necessary for filming in these culturally significant locations, as the state’s preservation laws ensure that filmmakers respect the history and integrity of these sacred sites. New Mexico’s appeal for filmmakers is not just limited to its locations; it also benefits from its strong support infrastructure, including production services, experienced crew members, and a long history of successful film and television productions. Major Hollywood films such as The Avengers and Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull have filmed in New Mexico, making use of the state’s diverse environments and cost-effective production services. These high-profile projects help cement New Mexico’s reputation as a top filming location.

research.title: Permits - Film Las Cruces
research.excerpt: Film Las Cruces will guide both production and government staff throughout the entire process, providing a streamlined experience. Contact Us …film and media production is an industry we continue to support. “As we work to increase the economic vitality for the City of Las Cruces, film and digital media production is an industry we continue to support. I am pleased to see productions benefiting from our talented workforce and scenic diversity,” said Las Cruces Mayor, Ken Miyagishima. Permit FAQs How much does a film permit cost? The filming permit application is free to submit and there will be no charges from Film Las Cruces. Direct services from the City of Las Cruces, Doña Ana County and the City of Anthony have fees. Give us a call or shoot us a message if you need more information. In what jurisdictions does Film Las Cruces process filming permits? Film Las Cruces is contracted with the City of Las Cruces, Doña Ana County and the City of Anthony to provide permitting assistance to film and digital media projects. We are happy to walk you through and point you in the right direction for all other permitting agencies throughout southern New Mexico; including White Sands National Park, Town of Mesilla, Bureau of Land Management, Spaceport America, Hatch, New Mexico Department of Transportation, and others. What kinds of filming activities do not require a permit? News and gathering of news related stories. Other types of documentaries not requiring the use of actors, models, sets, or props. Still not sure if your production requires a filming permit? Give us a call: 575-805-3456 What is a low impact/b-roll permit? A low impact/b-roll filming permit may be issued for documentary-style footage with a maximum of 8 total cast and crew on-site at any one time.

research.excerpt: Contact the New Mexico Film Office early for location scouting and support Secure insurance promptly to support permitting on public and tribal lands Plan for extreme temperature swings, dust, and high-altitude conditions Leverage local crew and vendors for authenticity and cost savings Respect Native American lands and cultural traditions Ready to Film in New Mexico? From the otherworldly dunes of White Sands to the vibrant streets of Albuquerque, the artistic soul of Santa Fe, and the majestic mountains of the north, New Mexico offers filmmakers unparalleled beauty, cultural depth, and production value. Let MovieInsure help protect your New Mexico production. Call 888-959-0772 today or request a quote online. We’re here to support your storytelling with reliable, affordable insurance tailored to the Land of Enchantment. Let’s create something magical in New Mexico! NEW MEXICO Tax Credits As-Of: June 2026 Tax Credit: 25-40% refundable (NO per-project caps) New Mexico offers 25% base refundable tax credit with bonuses for TV series/pilots, certified production facilities, local union crew, and rural filming—bringing effective rates to 40% in optimal scenarios. The refundable structure is critical: productions receive cash back regardless of in-state tax liability. New Mexico’s annual cap increased from $120M to $130M for fiscal 2025, with further increases planned to reach $160M by 2028. Per-project and per-person wage caps were removed, enabling large productions to access unlimited value. The state maintains exceptional production infrastructure: Netflix Studios Albuquerque, major facilities in Santa Fe and Las Cruces, established crew bases. Locations range from desert landscapes to high-altitude terrain to historic cities.
